mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in FEDFUNDS and a decline of at least 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with supply-side stress, which amplifies recession risk and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > +0.5% AND INDPRO < -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase of at least 1% in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer balance sheets, which boosts demand for goods and services and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly fall of at least 0.3 percentage points in UNRATE and a rise of at least 0.5% in FEDFUNDS signals a 'soft landing' attempt, where labor market weakness coincides with tightening policy; under these conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days are expected to be flat or slightly positive due to balanced risks.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < -0.3pp AND FEDFUNDS > +0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 3% in the RSAFS (retail sales) index signals a strong acceleration in consumer spending, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
